construct.claim: A sound typed code relation with a common coordinate section induces a four-operation typing of its source; NAE product requires exponentially many section-preserving charts.
construct.scope: Disjoint code blocks, common typed operations, arbitrary existential auxiliaries, sound decoding and fixed representatives for every source row.
construct.derivation: Closure survives conjunction and existential projection; compose block operations with fixed representatives and decoder; count proper NAE projections per chart.
unresolved_steps: Nonlocal transformations, context-dependent witness reconstruction and unrestricted universal coverage.
candidate_tests: All ternary typings, two-bit recodings, all NAE subrelations and small chart covers.

alternative.claim: A four-bit nonlinear decoder of a fixed affine gadget yields NAE exactly, but shared-block reuse can contradict a satisfiable source.
alternative.scope: Explicit translation gadget y=x XOR 1,z=x XOR 2, fixed common decoder.
alternative.derivation: Select u,v or u XOR v with two selector bits; enumerate six decoded patterns; compare two shared-variable atoms.
unresolved_steps: Compositional nonsection representations and total uniform transformation costs.
candidate_tests: All 16 affine rows, 64^3 sections, actual typed solver and shared-gadget composition.

objections: The section assumption is stronger than decoder surjectivity.
An explicit chart count does not bound SAT decision runtime.
Local nonlinear decoding may fail to glue.
counterexample_candidates: Affine NAE image with no common section; two satisfiable NAE atoms whose code conjunction is inconsistent.
critic.equivalence_audit: Exact source relation under section; decoded image equality alone does not imply compositional equivalence.
critic.barrier_audit: Restricted representation lower bound only, no universal complexity separation.
